summary: Verified the M365 error-surfacing fix end-to-end. Backend /api/m365/test correctly returns graph_ok=true and exchange_ok=false with a readable French exchange_error mentioning 'Exchange.ManageAsApp' and 'Exchange Administrator'. Backend /api/m365/push with s.lynch@champagneur.qc.ca returns applied_count=0 and failed[0].error with the same actionable 401 guidance (no null bytes). Frontend /app/m365: 'Tester la connexion' renders m365-test-result panel with 'Exchange (pousser) : échec' and the full guidance; selecting s.lynch and clicking 'Pousser' renders the red m365-push-errors panel with the email and the full French 401 guidance. Also confirmed a long-duration toast is shown.

issues: React console warning: 'Encountered two children with the same key k.charest@champagneur.qc.ca' — duplicate entry from Graph list; harmless but should be de-duped or key made unique.

action_items: (Optional/minor) De-duplicate M365 users list or use a compound React key to eliminate the duplicate-key console warning for k.charest@champagneur.qc.ca.
critical_code_review_comments: _exo_error() correctly decodes 401/403/other Exchange REST responses into actionable French guidance — good separation of concerns.
m365_test() now truly probes Exchange capability via Get-OrganizationConfig rather than only token acquisition — accurate capability reporting.
Frontend M365Connect surfaces per-user failures via data-testid m365-push-errors panel and toast — meets requirements.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The 401 from Exchange is EXPECTED (tenant Azure app lacks Exchange.ManageAsApp + Exchange Administrator role). All this iteration verified was that the failure is now cleanly surfaced. Both backend endpoints and the frontend panels display the exact French guidance mentioning 'Exchange.ManageAsApp' and 'Exchange Administrator'. Only cosmetic React duplicate-key warning remains in users list.
rca of the issue: N/A — verification of prior fix. Root cause of the underlying 401 is tenant-side: Azure app has valid token but no Exchange RBAC (Exchange.ManageAsApp) / Exchange Administrator role. The fix under test correctly decodes the Exchange REST error body and displays it verbatim in the UI.
